lead: Preterm labour is regular contractions with cervical change after 24 wk and before 37 completed weeks. It affects about 10% of births and is the leading cause of perinatal death and handicap. Management buys time for steroids and transfer, then plans a safe birth.
f: Extremely preterm 24–27⁺⁶ · very 28–31⁺⁶ · mild 32–36⁺⁶ wk · About a third each: after PPROM, spontaneous with intact membranes, iatrogenic · Threatened: contractions, cervix unchanged · Established: progressive dilatation · Four pathways: infection (commonest proven), bleeding, over-distension, cervical weakness · Risks: previous preterm birth, twins, polyhydramnios, uterine anomaly, cone biopsy, pyelonephritis, malaria, APH, age under 17 or over 35, short interval, smoking

Regular pains, backache, pelvic pressure, show, fluid, bleeding · The diagnosis is clinical; progressive cervical change is the proof · Sterile speculum first; digital VE only with intact membranes and praevia excluded · Fetal fibronectin negative: birth unlikely in 7–14 days · TV cervical length: over 15 mm labour unlikely; 15 mm or less birth likely within 7 days · Scan, CTG, HVS, urine culture, FBC, CRP · Differential: Braxton Hicks, pyelonephritis, red degeneration, abruption, appendicitis

tr: Contractions alone are not preterm labour: without cervical change most do not deliver
sc: 31 wk, tightenings, fFN negative → Birth unlikely in 7–14 days: no tocolysis

f: RDS (no surfactant): the commonest neonatal problem · Apnoea, chronic lung disease, PDA · IVH, periventricular leukomalacia → cerebral palsy · NEC, feeding problems, sepsis · Hypothermia, hypoglycaemia, jaundice · Retinopathy of prematurity, deafness

sc: Preterm baby with bloody stools and distension → NEC

f: Admit, confirm gestation, assess the fetus, tell parents and the neonatal team · Under 24 wk: counsel, comfort care, no steroids or tocolysis · 24–33⁺⁶ wk: steroids, nifedipine 48 h, GBS cover, MgSO₄ under 32 wk, transfer to a unit with NICU · 34 wk or more: no tocolysis, no steroids, let labour go on

sc: Preterm labour at 30 wk with fever and a tender uterus → No tocolysis: deliver
Preterm labour at 35 wk → No tocolysis, no steroids

f: Steroids 24–34 wk: dexamethasone 6 mg IM 12-hourly × 4 or betamethasone 12 mg IM × 2, 24 h apart · Work after 24 h, best at 2–7 days; reduce RDS, IVH, NEC, death · One course; raise insulin in diabetics; double the dose with enzyme inducers · Tocolysis 24–34 wk for 48 h only: buys time for steroids and transfer · Nifedipine first line (30 mg oral, then 20 mg 8-hourly; never sublingual) · Atosiban: fewest side effects, costly · Indomethacin under 32 wk only (ductus closure, oligohydramnios) · β-agonists: tachycardia, pulmonary oedema; not with heart disease or diabetes · Never two tocolytics

tr: No tocolysis with chorioamnionitis, fetal distress, IUFD, heavy APH, severe pre-eclampsia, advanced labour or over 34 wk
sc: Preterm labour with mitral stenosis → Nifedipine, not salbutamol

f: Under 32 wk when birth is expected within 24 h (also planned early birth) · 4 g IV over 20 min, then 1 g/h until birth or 24 h · Reduces cerebral palsy by about one third · Toxicity: lost reflexes, slow breathing → stop, calcium gluconate 10% 10 mL IV

Deliver where there is a neonatal unit; in-utero transfer is safer · GBS prophylaxis if positive or unknown: benzylpenicillin 3 g IV, then 1.8 g 4-hourly; not if the swab is negative · Continuous CTG once viable · Vaginal for cephalic; preterm breech often by CS · Forceps if needed; no ventouse before 32 wk, care at 32–36 wk · Delay cord clamping 1 min if well · Antibiotics with intact membranes only for GBS, UTI or BV

sc: Preterm 32 wk, delay in the second stage → Forceps, not ventouse

f: History-indicated cerclage at 12–14 wk after 3 or more mid-trimester losses or preterm births · 1–2 losses: TV cervical length every 2 wk at 16–24 wk; under 25 mm: cerclage or vaginal progesterone (200 mg nightly to 34 wk) · Emergency (rescue) cerclage for painless dilatation without infection · McDonald (simple) or Shirodkar (higher) · Remove at 36–37 wk, or at once with labour, ROM, APH or IUFD · Treat BV, bacteriuria, malaria; stop smoking; space pregnancies

sc: One previous birth at 30 wk; now 20 wk, cervix 18 mm → Cerclage or vaginal progesterone
